Je schopen vyhodnotit informace o produktech zveřejněných bankami včetně základních právních souvislostí plynoucích ze smluv. Student umí vyhodnotit základní parametry bankovního obchodu, jeho výnosnost, riziko a likviditu v praktických případech. Obsah předmětu: 1. Charakteristika obchodních bank, funkce bank. cs.label: [section] Požadavky na ukončení:
cs.content: Písemný zápočet. Obsahem zápočtu jsou praktické příklady, typově příklady řešené v seminářích. Složení zápočtu je předpokladem pro konání zkoušky. Krátká případová studie na zadané téma. Zpracování studie je fakultativní a získané body jsou bonusem k bodům získaným v zápočtu. Písemná zkouška obsahuje testové otázky s možností výběru odpovědi, posouzení správnosti výroků a výkladové otázky. Pro výsledné hodnocení je stanovena bodová stupnice. Dosažený součet bodů ze zápočtu (včetně fakultativně získaných bodů z případové studie) a ze zkoušky generuje výslednou známku: méně než 60 bodů F, 60 bodů a více E, 68 bodů a více D, 75 bodů a více C, 83 bodů a více B, 90 bodů a více A.

en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: The aim of the course is to equip students with knowledge about the banking market and banking products provided at consumers and companies. The student improves the knowledge in the field of banking. Student is able to assess information about products published by banks in the relation to the basic legal context of contracts. The student is able to evaluate the basic parameters of banking business, its profitability, risk and liquidity in practical cases. 1. Characteristics of commercial banks, functions of banks. (allowance 2/2) a. The essence of banking business. b. Basic functions of banks in the economic system. c. Specifics in the activities of commercial banks. 2. Banking systems, types of banks in banking systems (allowance 4/0) a. Historical outline of the development of banks and the banking environment. b. Banking systems and their basic attributes. c. Typology of banks in terms of their ownership and business focus. d. The banking system of the Czech Republic. 3. Nature and classification of banking transactions. (allowance 2/0) a. Nature and specifics of banking transactions b. Balance sheet recording of banking transactions. c. The essence and importance of business models in banking business. 4. Bank deposit transactions. (allowance 4/4) a. Legal regulation of deposit transactions in the Czech Republic. b. Selected types of deposit products, their characteristics, their use and development in the CR. c. Building savings in the Czech Republic. d. Deposit insurance, specifications for the EU and the Czech Republic. 5. Bank credit transactions. (allowance 8/6) a. Legal regulation of the credit relationship. b. The course of credit trade. c. Corporate bank loans in the Czech Republic, typology and development. d. Mortgage and consumer loans in the Czech Republic. 6. Organization and forms of payment system. (allowance 4/2) a. Functions and organization of the payment system. b. Selected payment instruments in the Czech banking sector. 7. Bank guarantee transactions. (allowance 2/0) 8. Trends in the development of banking and financial products. (allowance 2/0)

en.content: Written credit. The content of the credit is practical examples, type examples solved in seminars. Passing the credit is a prerequisite for taking the exam Short case studies on a given topic. The elaboration of the study is optional and the points obtained are a bonus to the points obtained in the credit. The written exam consist of test questions with the possibility of choosing the answer, assessment of the correctness of the statements and interpretive questions. A point scale is set for the final grade of the exam. The achieved sum of points consist of the points of credit (including optionally obtained points from the case study) and points of the exam. The total sum generates the final grade: less than 60 F points, 60 points and more E, 68 points and more D, 75 points and more C, 83 points and more B, 90 points and more A.
